Get BBL / DBBL Game Play-by-Play

Source: R/scb.R
scb_game_actions.Rd

Play-by-play of a finished game with shot x/y (BBL 2008-09 on, DBBL 2024-25 on).

Endpoint: GET https://api.basketball-bundesliga.de/games/{game_id}/stats (DBBL: the same route on https://api-1.dbbl.scb.world).

Usage

scb_game_actions(game_id, league = "bbl")

Arguments

game_id

(required) Game id (game_id in scb_games), e.g. 2006920 (BBL) or 10130 (DBBL). One sequence per league.

league

(default "bbl") League: bbl (men, easyCredit Basketball Bundesliga, api.basketball-bundesliga.de) or dbbl (women, Toyota Damen-Basketball-Bundesliga, api-1.dbbl.scb.world). The two share one API; game ids overlap, so a game is (league, game_id).

Value

A hoopR_data tibble: Play-by-play of a finished game with shot x/y (BBL 2008-09 on, DBBL 2024-25 on). An empty valid answer raises hoopR_no_data; the columns are always these, in this order (sdv-py scb_game_actions):

col_nametypedescription
leaguecharacterLeague the row belongs to: bbl (men) or dbbl (women); BBL and DBBL game ids overlap, so a game is (league, game_id).
game_idcharacterGame id, a string; unique within a league only (BBL and DBBL overlap), and not chronological.
action_idintegerAction id, an integer unique across games of a league.
order_idintegerChronological sequence of the action within the game.
action_identifiercharacterProvider action key <n>:<seq> (opaque; the first part is not the period).
periodintegerPeriod: 1-4 quarters, 5+ overtimes.
game_timecharacterGame clock as HH:MM:SS: in an action, the time LEFT in the period (00:10:00 at the start of a 10-minute quarter); in a game header, 00:00:00 in every sample.
seconds_leftintegerSeconds left in the period at the action: game_time as seconds.
real_timecharacterWall-clock time of the action, ISO 8601 UTC. Pre-2011 games carry a placeholder: local midnight of the game day (23:00 UTC the day before) on every row.
typecharacterAction type; see the action-type table. Records and videos use their own type (see those routes).
qualifierscharacterAction qualifiers (shot kind, rebound side, foul kind, turnover kind); see the qualifier table.
is_successfullogicalMade / successful (shots, free throws); for other types see the action-type table.
season_team_idcharacterSeason-team id; equal to the club teamId in every sample (BBL 2005-2026, DBBL 2024-2026).
sidecharacterhome or guest (the away side), for the team the row belongs to.
season_player_idcharacterSeason-player id: one player's engagement with one club (kept across seasons while he stays, new after a move; see README). Joins to box-score seasonPlayer.id, action seasonPlayerId and /season-players/{seasonPlayerId}. Null on team and period rows.
assisting_season_player_idcharacterSeason-player id of the assisting player; only on assisted made shots. Joins to box-score seasonPlayer.id and action seasonPlayerId.
shot_xintegerShot x on the site's half-court chart (0-280 across, 140 through the rim); null without a location. Scale and orientation unverified.
shot_yintegerShot y along the court from behind the baseline (rim near 45, arc top near 147); null without a location. Scale and orientation unverified.
home_team_pointsintegerHome score after this action; only on scoring actions.
guest_team_pointsintegerGuest score after this action; only on scoring actions.

Details

  • Unofficial use of a public source: these wrappers read the front-end API of the German Bundesliga sites (easycredit-bbl.de, toyota-dbbl.de), run by SCB; payloads are not redistributed as release assets.

  • Legal notice: the BBL Impressum forbids storing BBL content (Inhalte) in an information system without BBL's written permission. That is a copyright term, not a robots rule (the API host has no robots.txt). The owner reviewed it and accepted the intake (2026-10-12 ruling); keep requests slow (the runtime waits at least 1 s per host) and raise any published data release with the owner. The DBBL host is the same operator and API; its site notice was not separately reviewed.

  • Both hosts need two headers: a constant x-api-key and an x-api-secret that rotates. The runtime derives the secret on first use from the key embedded in an easycredit-bbl.de page (reversed, : turned into -) and never logs or returns it. The derivation was reverse-engineered from observed requests and responses and has not been checked against the site's own front-end code; if the site changes how it signs requests, every call fails with hoopR_asset_fetch.

  • Id key spaces: seasonId is the START year (2025 = 2025-26), so a wrapper's END-year season is sent as season - 1. Teams are keyed by teamId (seasonTeamId equals it in every sample). seasonPlayerId is per player per season and per club (a player traded mid-season has two); realPlayerId is the person. playerId is ambiguous (the seasonPlayerId in box scores, records and /season-players; the person in /transfers). Game ids are strings.

  • Errors are classed conditions: hoopR_no_data (404, 204, a 400 "not a valid" id, no rows, a box score of a game not yet started), hoopR_bad_request (a bad argument, another 400 / 422) and hoopR_asset_fetch (a refused secret after one re-derive, any other non-2xx, an HTML / non-JSON / error-shaped body, a truncated page, a body for another game, season, club or league, a box score still in play), all inheriting hoopR_error. Wrappers raise; they never return an empty frame.

See also

Other SCB Functions: scb_game(), scb_game_players(), scb_game_teams(), scb_games(), scb_games_recent(), scb_player_statistics(), scb_playoff_games(), scb_playoff_series(), scb_records_per_game(), scb_records_season_averages(), scb_referees(), scb_season_player(), scb_season_players(), scb_season_teams(), scb_seasons(), scb_standings(), scb_team(), scb_team_rosters(), scb_team_seasons(), scb_team_statistics(), scb_transfers(), scb_transfers_teams()
